front: Which ratios are positive in each quadrant?
back: Q1 all, Q2 sin, Q3 tan, Q4 cos.

front: sin and cos of π/6, π/4, π/3?
Ambiguous case of the sine rule?
back: sin B = k gives B and 180° − B; keep both if the angles sum < 180°.

front: Are exact trig values in the formula booklet?
back: No — the values for $0, \frac\pi6, \frac\pi4, \frac\pi3, \frac\pi2$ must be memorised (Paper 1 has no calculator).
$-1 \le \sin\theta, \cos\theta \le 1$; $\tan\theta$ takes any real value but is undefined when $\cos\theta = 0$.
The point $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$ lies on the unit circle $x^2 + y^2 = 1$.

front: Meaning of a negative angle or an angle above $2\pi$ on the unit circle?
back: Negative: measured clockwise. Adding $2\pi$ returns to the same point, so values repeat every $2\pi$.
$\sin B = \frac{10\sin30^\circ}6 = \frac56$: $B \approx 56.4^\circ$ or $123.6^\circ$. Both valid ($30^\circ + 123.6^\circ < 180^\circ$): two triangles.

front: When can the ambiguous case arise?
back: Only when using the sine rule to find an angle from two sides and a non-included angle (SSA). It never arises with the cosine rule.
